data.description:
Filed out of TB-18, which named this as an out-of-scope opportunity. Distinct from TB-18: that ticket makes the absent per-call usage channel *legible* (renders `n/a` instead of `no`). This ticket asks whether a real, populated cache signal at session grain should be used at all.

`_is_cache_hit(usage)` (passive.py:174) consults only per-call `message.usage`. hermes has none — not in the SQLite adapter (ABSENT_BY_SCHEMA) and not in `--format trace` (ABSENT_BY_EXPORT). So every hermes call counts as a cache MISS today, from both paths.

But hermes does record cache data, at SESSION grain.

MEASURED against the live archive (2026-07-10, read-only, all four databases — including `aphrodite-mood`, which was unreadable until the WAL fix in TB-18 Task 0 landed):

  profile              sessions  cache_read>0   messages  token_count non-null
  .hermes                   795           721       6781                     0
  aphrodite-mood             34            29       2006                     0
  light-mood                 28            20        746                     0
  tech-interviewing           6             6        644                     0
  TOTAL                     863           776      10177                     0

776 / 863 sessions (90%) carry `cache_read_tokens > 0`. `messages.token_count` is null in all 10,177 rows, confirming the grain is session, not message.

THE HARD PART is attribution, not availability. A session-grain figure cannot be attributed to an individual tool call without inventing a denominator. Do NOT divide by tool_call_count and report a per-call rate — that fabricates precision the data does not have, which is the same class of error TB-18 exists to fix.

CANDIDATE SHAPES (not chosen):
  a. Report cache as a session-grain caveat line for hermes, alongside the per-call flag for claude, and never mix the two in one column.
  b. Extend UsageProvenance with a PRESENT_AT_SESSION_GRAIN member so the render rule can say "measured, but not at this grain".
  c. Leave `n/a` (TB-18 outcome) and document that hermes cache data exists but is out-of-grain for a per-call report.

Depends on TB-18 landing first: UsageProvenance and the four-case render rule are the seam this would extend.

ACCEPTANCE. Either hermes cache data reaches the report at a grain it actually has, or the report states that session-grain cache data exists and is deliberately not attributed per call. What must not survive: a report implying hermes achieved a 0% cache-hit rate.
data.title: hermes sessions report 100% cache-miss: session-grain cache_read_tokens is never consulted

data.note: TB-18 introduces UsageProvenance and the four-case render rule; TB-20 extends that seam to session-grain cache data. TB-18 lands first.

data.body: RUN-2 INTAKE (orchestrator): depends_on TB-18 (hard link) — TB-18 Task 3 rewrites the passive cache render into the four-case form (yes/no/n-a/n-a-star) and adds ToolStats.usage_missing; TB-20's session-grain cache_read_tokens consultation must build on that render, not race it. Evidence pinned during TB-18 investigation: messages.token_count is NULL on all 10,177 rows across the 4 archive DBs; usage lives on the sessions row (788 sessions, 714 with cache_read_tokens greater than 0). DBs open read-only ALWAYS (mode=ro; immutable fallback only when no -wal sidecar — see _connect after TB-18 Task 0). DOCS phase authors SPEC criterion S32 + EVALUATION row + BUILDPLAN row. Branch off origin/main AFTER TB-18's PR #20 merges (rebase onto it if it hasn't).

plan self-review: PASS, 1 finding (non-blocking) — verified cache_read_tokens column exists with zero NULLs across all 4 live profile DBs (803/34/28/8 sessions), retiring the risk of a runtime OperationalError on an older-schema profile; field stays nullable defensively with an explicit NULL fixture test since no live row exercises that arm. No shape change to the design (session-grain caveat line, orthogonal to UsageProvenance). Also flagged: orchestrator-intake comment says branch off main/rebase onto #20, which contradicts actual git state (already cut from parent branch) and the delegator prompt's no-rebase rule -- following the prompt.
working against origin/chore/add-hermes-cli-export-plan @ 5c74901d4fec768654ae4d6fea8777a547f39f87 (branch tb-20-cache-read currently identical to parent tip, clean tree)

COMPLETION (TB-20): PR #22 opened, base chore/add-hermes-cli-export-plan, MERGEABLE, head 8cb7dd3 != base 5c74901. Status -> review; stops here per delegator contract (orchestrator owns merge).

WHAT SHIPPED: session-grain hermes cache_read_tokens now reaches the report as an Agent Breakdown caveat line ("N of M sessions carry session-grain cache_read_tokens > 0"), orthogonal to and never mixed with the per-call cache_assisted column (TB-18's four-case n/a/n/a*/no/yes render is byte-for-byte untouched). UsageProvenance was not extended -- candidate shape (a) from the ticket was chosen over (b), with rationale in the plan. No per-call rate is ever fabricated: the two new AgentStats counters increment once per session, never per call, verified by a dedicated test and by real-corpus evidence.

TESTS: 205 -> 218 passed (+13), 1 pre-existing skip unchanged, 0 failures. ruff clean throughout. mypy --strict held at the 38-error pre-existing baseline, 0 new errors, across all 7 feature commits.

BEFORE/AFTER (live hermes archive, read-only, 94 sessions / 1455 calls via agentsview discovery -- identical both runs): BEFORE (parent branch, disposable temp worktree) shows no session-grain signal anywhere. AFTER (this branch) adds "hermes: 91 of 94 sessions carry session-grain cache_read_tokens > 0 (S32: session grain only -- not attributable to individual tool calls)."; Tool Leaderboard cache_assisted stays n/a in both, unchanged.

DEVIATIONS (flagged, both also in the PR body):
1. Board's orchestrator-intake comment said branch off main/rebase onto #20 after merge -- contradicts actual git state (branch already cut from the parent per the delegator prompt) and the prompt's explicit no-rebase rule. Followed the prompt/actual state; flagged in the plan self-review comment and here.
2. Three of the delegator prompt's pinned install facts were stale against this lattice v0.2.0 install: `lattice show` rejects `--actor` (only some subcommands accept it -- worked around by omitting it there); `lattice attach --role` only accepts `review`, not `validation` (used a titled note attachment instead); `lattice attach --type url` doesn't exist (valid types are conversation/file/log/note/prompt/reference -- used `reference`). None blocked the work; all three are one-line CLI-shape corrections, not design conflicts.

No Critical/Major findings in code self-review (one Minor -- a redundant double loop in render_report -- found and fixed in the same session, commit 8cb7dd3).
